title: Coding-Agent Work-Plan Template
summary: Records the information required to correct the coding-agent work-plan template without rewriting unaffected material. The substantive correction remains blocked because the existing resource and replacement source were not supplied.

The replacement first-party HTTPS source and its publication metadata

sections.title: Can the correction proceed?
paragraphs: No. An intermediate practitioner cannot safely complete this correction from the supplied material. The existing resource object, the replacement first-party HTTPS source, and the mapping from that source to affected content are UNKNOWN and therefore omitted rather than reconstructed.

The cited source under review is content/resources/coding-agents/coding-agent-work-plan-template.json. Whether it moved, exceeded its review cadence, or experienced both events is UNKNOWN. What the source change affected is also UNKNOWN because neither the former source content nor the existing guide was supplied.

This object must not be treated as evidence that the original guide was preserved. A correction-only update requires the existing object verbatim so unchanged fields, sections, procedures, and wording can remain untouched.

sections.title: Correction procedure
paragraphs: Step 1. Obtain the existing JSON object verbatim from the target path. If it cannot be obtained, stop and request it from the catalogue maintainer rather than reconstructing titles, metadata, sections, or procedures.

Step 2. Establish whether the cited source moved, passed its review cadence, or both. Record the former location, replacement HTTPS URL, source title, publisher of record, and actual verification date. If any item is unavailable or the replacement URL does not open directly over HTTPS, stop and request a verified first-party source.

Step 3. Compare the former and replacement source content and identify every existing statement, instruction, and metadata value affected by the change. If the comparison does not establish the impact, mark the impact UNKNOWN and request an editorial change notice rather than changing guide content.

Step 4. Apply only the established corrections to the existing object. Preserve every unaffected value and passage exactly. If a proposed edit cannot be traced to the source comparison or a schema requirement, remove that edit from the correction.

Step 5. Validate the completed object against the platform Resource schema and check identifier uniqueness across resources, modules, and learning paths. If the schema or catalogue identifier set is unavailable, stop publication and request both from the catalogue maintainer.

The JSON serialization reference listed in the sources defines the underlying data format. It does not establish any coding-agent work-plan stages, technical procedures, products, commands, or configuration keys, so none are asserted here.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is the original resource object, a replacement first-party HTTPS source with complete publisher and verification metadata, a source comparison showing the affected statements, and a correction-only comparison showing no unrelated edits.

Verify the result by confirming that the identifier remains coding-agent-work-plan-template, the object satisfies every required Resource field, exactly three sections remain, and all unaffected values and wording match the original object. If any unaffected difference appears, revert it and repeat the comparison.

Open every final source URL directly over HTTPS and compare the corrected statements with the cited source. If a URL fails, redirects to an unsuitable location, or does not support a corrected statement, do not publish; obtain a resolvable first-party replacement and repeat verification.

The expected corrected guide content is UNKNOWN until the missing baseline and source evidence are supplied. Catalogue-wide identifier uniqueness is also UNKNOWN until the shared identifier set is checked.
